All songs with the exception of "Murders in the Rue Morgue" and "Prodigal Son" were written before the recording of Iron Maiden's debut album. "Wrathchild" is one of the first songs composed by Iron Maiden, dating back to 1976. It was first recorded in 1979 and included on the "Metal for Muthas" split (1980). None of the other songs had been recorded in-studio before, though a live recording of "Drifter" appears on the B-side of the single "Sanctuary".

"Wrathchild" was originally planned to be recorded for the debut album, but was ultimately shelved. When Bruce Dickinson rejoined Iron Maiden in 1999, he recorded new vocals for the song that were dubbed over the original recording and used as a hidden track on the "Ed Hunter" compilation. This version is better known as "Wrathchild '99".

"Murders in the Rue Morgue" is inspired by Edgar Allan Poe's story of the same name.

The song "Killers" originally had different lyrics, which can be heard on the "Live at the Rainbow" video.

"Twilight Zone" was recorded during the album sessions, but only appeared on the North American and Japanese versions of the album. It was released as a double A-side single with "Wrathchild" in the UK, and was belatedly added to the standard album tracklist when the Iron Maiden catalogue was reissued in 1998.

The songs "Wrathchild", "Killers" and "Twilight Zone" were used for Bruce Dickinson's 1981 audition tape.

Recording information:

Recorded at Battery Studios, London.
